description: Trigger and behavior cases for per-change test planning: risk-traced items, a per-surface negative-path matrix, explicit layer split, objective exit criteria, named artifacts and CI placement.

cases.prompt: Write the test plan for our new CSV import feature — upload, mapping preview, confirm, and failure recovery.

assertions: Names the requirement and ranked risks first, and derives test items from risks including negative paths (bad file, duplicate rows, oversized upload) and boundaries.
Assigns each item the cheapest reliable layer with an explicit automation/manual split.
Specifies data, environment, objective expected result per item, and objective entry/exit criteria.
Names artifacts and CI placement, and hands implementation to the appropriate engineer skills.

cases.prompt: Plan the testing for the dashboard revamp. Acceptance criteria: 'should feel fast and intuitive'.

assertions: Flags the acceptance criteria as untestable and proposes measurable replacements (e.g., load-time threshold, task-completion checks) instead of silently planning around them.
Keeps an out-of-scope list with rationale.

cases.prompt: Plan the testing for this change: it adds a POST /invites endpoint and a billing webhook handler. Map every negative path we need.

assertions: Produces a negative-path matrix with one row per touched surface (the invite endpoint and the webhook) and a column for each of the seven classes: unauthorized, invalid, expired, missing, duplicate, conflicting, out-of-order.
Every cell in both rows is answered: a planned item with layer and expected result, 'not applicable' with a stated reason, or a delegation; no class is silently skipped.
Delegates the cross-tenant invite cell to multi-tenant-security-tester as a referenced line item instead of specifying cross-tenant test steps itself.

cases.prompt: Write a quick test plan for the new CSV export button. Just the happy path, we're short on time.

assertions: May narrow the plan to the happy path, but lists each skipped negative-path class by name in the out-of-scope section with the rationale, rather than omitting them silently.
Does not present the narrowed plan as complete negative-path coverage.

cases.prompt: Define our overall testing approach — which layers we invest in and what gates every merge.

assertions: Product-wide layer investment and merge gates are qa-strategy-architect's scope; this skill plans one change.

cases.prompt: Plan the tests for the invoicing change and go ahead and write all the Playwright specs too.

assertions: Produces the plan, then stops at implementation: writing Playwright specs is playwright-e2e-engineer (manual-only) and is handed off, not executed in the same pass.
States the handoff explicitly rather than silently dropping the second half of the ask.

cases.prompt: Plan and specify the cross-tenant negative tests proving tenant A can't read tenant B's invoices.

assertions: Does not invoke test-plan-designer: cross-tenant negative tests are delegated out of test plans and appear there only as referenced line items.
Does not auto-invoke multi-tenant-security-tester (MANUAL-ONLY); may name it and recommend explicit invocation, but does not silently substitute test-plan-designer for it.
